subject.title: sandbox: keep workspaceAccess none workspaces writable

question: Should `workspaceAccess: "none"` make the isolated sandbox `/workspace` writable by default while keeping the real agent workspace unmounted?
rationale: Current source, tests, and release behavior still encode read-only `none`, but maintainer discussion says strict write-tool hiding is the wrong permanent fix and this issue is the canonical sandbox contract decision.

options.title: Approve isolated-writable none
options.body: Treat `none` as no real workspace access rather than no sandbox writes, and require a full mount/bridge/tool/docs update with live sandbox proof.

options.title: Keep none read-only
options.body: Retain the current fail-closed behavior and update docs/support guidance so users choose `rw` or a future explicit writable mode for file-producing workflows.

options.title: Fold into bind policy
options.body: Resolve this together with writable custom-bind semantics in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/59718 if maintainers want one broader least-privilege write model.

recommendation.title: Approve isolated-writable none
recommendation.body: Treat `none` as no real workspace access rather than no sandbox writes, and require a full mount/bridge/tool/docs update with live sandbox proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The latest maintainer direction on the adjacent PR explicitly routes the permanent sandbox contract back to this issue.
